sections.title: Regulatory & Growth
sections.subtitle: APS, Pinnacle West's regulated utility subsidiary, earns a fixed return set by the Arizona Corporation Commission (ACC) rather than a market-determined margin -- these charts are the regulated-utility equivalent of the margin and growth charts above.

charts.title: Retail Customer Growth & Weather-Normalized Sales Growth
charts.annotation: Weather-normalized sales growth strips out hot/cold-weather swings to isolate the underlying demand trend -- the number management points to as evidence of Arizona data-center and large-load growth.

charts.title: Allowed vs Requested ROE (APS)
charts.annotation: Authorized ROE only moves when a new rate case settles -- it held at 9.55% from the 2022 settlement until the pending 2025 case, which requests 10.70% on a $12.5bn rate base.

charts.title: CapEx: Actual vs 3-Year Plan
charts.annotation: Guidance and the 3-year plan are management's disclosed figures, not audited actuals -- a rising plan is the rate-base growth the ROE is earned on.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Pinnacle West Capital Corporation: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Pinnacle West Capital Corporation: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

growthDrivers.title: Retail customer and weather-normalized sales growth
growthDrivers.content:
Retail customer growth is the YoY change in the number of metered accounts APS serves. Weather-normalized sales growth adjusts electricity sales for temperature so a hot or cool year doesn't mask the underlying trend.

For Pinnacle West Capital Corporation: Arizona is one of the fastest-growing US states for both population and large-load siting (data centers, semiconductor and advanced-manufacturing plants) in APS's exclusive service territory. Weather-normalized sales growth running well above customer growth (as in 9M-2026) signals that existing and new large-load customers are using more power per connection, not just that more houses were added -- the data-center demand story management is selling.

What to watch:

  • Sales growth decoupling from customer growth (large-load effect)
  • Regulatory lag: new large-load demand raises revenue before the next rate case lets APS recover the capex it required

rateCase.title: Rate case: allowed vs requested ROE
rateCase.content:
APS is a regulated monopoly: instead of a market-set margin, the Arizona Corporation Commission (ACC) periodically sets a rate base (the capital APS is allowed to earn a return on) and an authorized ROE (the percentage return it can earn on that rate base) in a rate case. Rates charged to customers are built to recover costs plus that allowed return.

For Pinnacle West Capital Corporation: the 2022 settlement set authorized ROE at 9.55%, effective March 2024. APS's pending 2025 rate case requests 10.70% ROE on a $12.5bn rate base; a decision is expected around December 2026. The gap between requested and allowed is the single biggest swing factor in near-term earnings -- every 0.1 percentage point the ACC trims off the request is a direct, permanent cut to the return APS earns on its capital base.

What to watch:

  • The ACC's final decision versus the 10.70% request
  • Whether the new rate base is close to the $12.5bn requested
  • Interim mechanisms (fuel/purchased-power adjustors) that let APS recover some costs between full rate cases

capexGuidance.title: CapEx guidance and the 3-year plan
capexGuidance.content:
Next-year capex guidance and the 3-year capex plan are management's own disclosed spending figures, shown alongside actual reported CapEx.

For Pinnacle West Capital Corporation: a regulated utility's earnings growth comes almost entirely from growing its rate base, which it does by spending capex on generation, transmission and distribution and then asking the ACC to let it earn its allowed ROE on that larger base. A rising 3-year plan (from $6.0bn to $7.95bn across FY2023-FY2025 guidance) is APS funding the Arizona demand-growth story; it is also the capital the next rate case has to recover, and new spending earns nothing until the ACC approves it into rate base.

What to watch:

  • Guidance revised up mid-year (demand running ahead of plan) versus cut (permitting or supply-chain delay)
  • How the plan is financed -- more debt and equity issuance dilutes existing shareholders' claim on the larger rate base

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Pinnacle West Capital Corporation: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Pinnacle West Capital Corporation: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Pinnacle West Capital Corporation: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Pinnacle West Capital Corporation: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Pinnacle West Capital Corporation: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Pinnacle West Capital Corporation: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Pinnacle West Capital Corporation: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Pinnacle West Capital Corporation: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
